exercises.title: Three vector norms
exercises.description: Compute $\|x\|_1$, $\|x\|_2$ and $\|x\|_\infty$ for $x = (1, -2, 2)^T$ and check $\|x\|_\infty \le \|x\|_2 \le \|x\|_1$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Sum of magnitudes, root of the sum of squares, largest magnitude.

Step 3: Check
$2 \le 3 \le 5$ ✓.

Step 4: Takeaway: What matters
Do not forget magnitudes: negative entries count positively.

exercises.title: Row-sum and column-sum norms
exercises.description: Determine $\|A\|_1$ and $\|A\|_\infty$ for $A = \begin{pmatrix}2&-1&0\\1&3&2\\-4&1&1\end{pmatrix}$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
$\|A\|_1$ = largest column sum, $\|A\|_\infty$ = largest row sum (of magnitudes).

Step 3: Rows
Row sums: $3$, $6$, $6$. So $\|A\|_\infty = 6$.

Step 4: Takeaway: What matters
Mnemonic: the 1 stands “upright” (columns), the $\infty$ “lies down” (rows).

exercises.title: cond of a diagonal matrix
exercises.description: Compute $\mathrm{cond}_\infty$ for $D = \mathrm{diag}(1, 10, 100)$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
$D^{-1} = \mathrm{diag}(1, 0.1, 0.01)$.

Step 2: Norms
$\|D\|_\infty = 100$, $\|D^{-1}\|_\infty = 1$.

Step 3: Result
$\mathrm{cond}_\infty(D) = 100\cdot 1 = 100$ (= largest / smallest entry; the same for $\mathrm{cond}_1$ and $\mathrm{cond}_2$).

Step 4: Takeaway: What matters
For diagonal matrices you read off the condition directly: ratio of the largest to the smallest magnitude.

exercises.title: cond of an orthogonal matrix
exercises.description: Show $\mathrm{cond}_2(Q) = 1$ for $Q = \begin{pmatrix}0.6&-0.8\\0.8&0.6\end{pmatrix}$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
$Q$ is orthogonal: $Q^TQ = I$, so $Q^{-1} = Q^T$ and $\|Qx\|_2 = \|x\|_2$.

Step 2: Orthogonality
$Q^TQ = \begin{pmatrix}0.36 + 0.64&-0.48 + 0.48\\-0.48 + 0.48&0.64 + 0.36\end{pmatrix} = I$ ✓.

Step 3: Norms
$\|Q\|_2 = \sqrt{\lambda_{\max}(Q^TQ)} = \sqrt1 = 1$ and $\|Q^{-1}\|_2 = \|Q^T\|_2 = 1$.

Step 4: Result
$\mathrm{cond}_2(Q) = 1\cdot 1 = 1$ – the best possible condition.

Step 5: Takeaway: What matters
Orthogonal transformations do not amplify errors – that is why QR (4.5) is so stable.

exercises.title: Checking norm properties
exercises.description: Is (a) $N_1(x) = |x_1|$ and (b) $N_2(x) = |x_1| + 2|x_2|$ a norm on $\mathbb R^2$?
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Check definiteness, homogeneity and the triangle inequality.

Step 2: (a)
For $x = (0, 1)^T \ne 0$ we have $N_1(x) = 0$: definiteness violated – not a norm (only a seminorm).

Step 3: (b)
$N_2(x) = 0 \iff x_1 = x_2 = 0$ ✓. $N_2(\alpha x) = |\alpha|N_2(x)$ ✓. The triangle inequality follows from $|a + b| \le |a| + |b|$ in each component ✓. So a (weighted 1-)norm.

Step 4: Takeaway: What matters
All three properties are needed. Without definiteness it is only a seminorm.

exercises.title: Matching unit balls
exercises.description: Which of the points $(1,0)$, $(0.5,0.5)$, $(0.7,0.7)$ lie in the unit balls of the 1-, 2- and $\infty$-norm (boundary included)?
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Compute the three norms of each point and compare with $1$.

Step 2: (1, 0)
Norms $1, 1, 1$: in all three balls (on the boundary).

Step 3: (0.5, 0.5)
$\|\cdot\|_1 = 1$, $\|\cdot\|_2 = 0.707$, $\|\cdot\|_\infty = 0.5$: in all three balls (on the boundary of the 1-ball).

Step 4: (0.7, 0.7)
$\|\cdot\|_1 = 1.4 > 1$, $\|\cdot\|_2 = 0.990 \le 1$, $\|\cdot\|_\infty = 0.7 \le 1$: only in the 2- and $\infty$-ball, not in the rhombus.

Step 5: Takeaway: What matters
We have $B_1 \subset B_2 \subset B_\infty$: rhombus ⊂ circle ⊂ square.

exercises.title: Inverse and cond∞ (2×2)
exercises.description: For $A = \begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$ compute the inverse and $\mathrm{cond}_\infty(A)$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
2×2 inverse: $A^{-1} = \frac{1}{\det A}\begin{pmatrix}d&-b\\-c&a\end{pmatrix}$.

Step 2: Inverse
$\det A = 2 - 1 = 1$, $A^{-1} = \begin{pmatrix}1&-1\\-1&2\end{pmatrix}$ (check: $AA^{-1} = I$ ✓).

Step 4: Result
$\mathrm{cond}_\infty(A) = 3\cdot 3 = 9$ – well-conditioned.

Step 5: Takeaway: What matters
For 2×2 the inverse takes one line – ideal for exam problems.

exercises.title: Decimal-digit rule of thumb
exercises.description: A system has $\mathrm{cond}(A) = 10^6$, the data are accurate to $10^{-8}$. How accurate is the solution (relative) at most guaranteed?
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Perturbation theorem: error $\le \mathrm{cond}\cdot$ data error.

Step 2: Computation
$10^6\cdot 10^{-8} = 10^{-2}$: relative error up to $1\%$.

Step 3: Digits
Of $8$ digits of data accuracy $\log_{10}10^6 = 6$ are lost: only about $2$ digits are secured.

Step 4: Takeaway: What matters
Arithmetic precision minus $\log_{10}\mathrm{cond}$ = valid decimal digits.

exercises.title: Spectral norm of symmetric matrices
exercises.description: Compute $\|A\|_2$ and $\mathrm{cond}_2(A)$ for $A = \begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}$ and for $B = \begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1.0001\end{pmatrix}$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
For symmetric matrices $\|A\|_2 = \max|\lambda_i|$ and $\mathrm{cond}_2 = \max|\lambda|/\min|\lambda|$.

Step 2: Matrix A
Eigenvalues: $\lambda^2 - 4\lambda + 3 = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = 3, 1$. $\|A\|_2 = 3$, $\mathrm{cond}_2(A) = 3$.

Step 4: Result
$\mathrm{cond}_2(B) = \frac{2.00005}{0.00005} \approx 40002$ – similar to $\mathrm{cond}_\infty = 40004$.

Step 5: Takeaway: What matters
All induced norms give condition numbers of the same order of magnitude (norm equivalence).

exercises.title: Applying the perturbation theorem
exercises.description: For $A = \begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{pmatrix}$ ($\mathrm{cond}_\infty = 21$), $b = (5, 11)^T$ ($x = (1,2)^T$) $b$ is perturbed by $\Delta b$ with $\|\Delta b\|_\infty \le 0.01$. Estimate $\|\Delta x\|_\infty$ and check it for $\Delta b = (0.01, -0.01)^T$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
$\dfrac{\|\Delta x\|}{\|x\|} \le \mathrm{cond}(A)\dfrac{\|\Delta b\|}{\|b\|}$.

Step 2: Bound
$\dfrac{\|\Delta b\|_\infty}{\|b\|_\infty} = \dfrac{0.01}{11} = 9.09\cdot10^{-4}$. Times $21$: $0.0191$. With $\|x\|_\infty = 2$: $\|\Delta x\|_\infty \le 0.0382$.

Step 3: Check
$\Delta x = A^{-1}\Delta b = \begin{pmatrix}-2&1\\1.5&-0.5\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}0.01\\-0.01\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}-0.03\\0.02\end{pmatrix}$, $\|\Delta x\|_\infty = 0.03 \le 0.0382$ ✓.

Step 4: Takeaway: What matters
The bound is sharp up to a constant: it overestimates only by $27\%$ here.

exercises.title: Reworking the key example (variant)
exercises.description: Let $A = \begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1.001\end{pmatrix}$. Solve $Ax = b$ for $b = (2, 2.001)^T$ and $\tilde b = (2, 2.002)^T$, determine $\mathrm{cond}_\infty(A)$ and check the perturbation theorem.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Solve two systems, $A^{-1}$ for the condition.

Step 3: Condition
$A^{-1} = 1000\begin{pmatrix}1.001&-1\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}$, $\|A^{-1}\|_\infty = 2001$, $\|A\|_\infty = 2.001$. $\mathrm{cond}_\infty = 2.001\cdot 2001 = 4004$.

Step 4: Perturbation theorem
Relative data change $\frac{0.001}{2.001} = 5\cdot10^{-4}$. Bound $4004\cdot 5\cdot 10^{-4} = 2.0$. Actual relative change: $\frac{\|\Delta x\|_\infty}{\|x\|_\infty} = \frac{1}{1} = 1 \le 2$ ✓.

Step 5: Takeaway: What matters
A factor of $10$ larger angle (now $10^{-3}$ instead of $10^{-4}$): condition $\frac{1}{10}$ – the solution is still unstable.

exercises.title: Residual versus error
exercises.description: For $A = \begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1.0001\end{pmatrix}$, $b = (2, 2.0001)^T$ and $\tilde x = (2, 0)^T$: compute residual and error and compare the ratios.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
$r = b - A\tilde x$; error $x - \tilde x$ with $x = (1,1)^T$.

Step 3: Error
$x - \tilde x = (-1, 1)^T$, relative $\frac{\|x - \tilde x\|_\infty}{\|x\|_\infty} = 1$.

Step 4: Comparison
Ratio error/residual $= 1/(5\cdot 10^{-5}) = 2\cdot 10^{4}$ $\le \mathrm{cond} = 40004$ ✓.

Step 5: Takeaway: What matters
The residual is a good error indicator only if $\mathrm{cond}(A)$ is small.

exercises.title: Hilbert matrix
exercises.description: Compute $\mathrm{cond}_\infty$ of the Hilbert matrix $H_2 = \begin{pmatrix}1&\frac12\\\frac12&\frac13\end{pmatrix}$ and state $\mathrm{cond}_\infty(H_3) = 748$. How many digits are lost for $H_3$?
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Inverse: $\det H_2 = \frac13 - \frac14 = \frac1{12}$.

Step 2: Inverse
$H_2^{-1} = 12\begin{pmatrix}\frac13&-\frac12\\-\frac12&1\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}4&-6\\-6&12\end{pmatrix}$.

Step 3: Norms
$\|H_2\|_\infty = 1.5$, $\|H_2^{-1}\|_\infty = 18$. $\mathrm{cond}_\infty(H_2) = 27$.

Step 4: H₃
$\mathrm{cond}_\infty(H_3) = 748 \approx 10^{2.9}$: about $3$ digits are lost. $H_3^{-1} = \begin{pmatrix}9&-36&30\\-36&192&-180\\30&-180&180\end{pmatrix}$ has integer but large entries.

Step 5: Takeaway: What matters
The condition of the Hilbert matrix grows exponentially ($\approx e^{3.5n}$): $H_{10}$ has $\approx 10^{13}$.

exercises.title: cond(αA) = cond(A)
exercises.description: Show $\mathrm{cond}(\alpha A) = \mathrm{cond}(A)$ for $\alpha \ne 0$ and explain why $\det A$ does not measure conditioning (example $A = 10^{-10}I_2$).
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Norms are homogeneous: $\|\alpha A\| = |\alpha|\|A\|$.

Step 2: Proof
$(\alpha A)^{-1} = \frac1\alpha A^{-1}$. So $\mathrm{cond}(\alpha A) = |\alpha|\|A\|\cdot\frac{1}{|\alpha|}\|A^{-1}\| = \|A\|\|A^{-1}\| = \mathrm{cond}(A)$.

Step 4: Conversely
$B = \begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1.0001\end{pmatrix}$ has $\det B = 10^{-4}$ and $\mathrm{cond} = 40004$. The value of the determinant depends on the scale, the condition does not.

Step 5: Takeaway: What matters
The determinant is a poor indicator for “nearly singular” – the condition number is the right one.

exercises.title: cond(AB) ≤ cond(A)·cond(B)
exercises.description: Prove $\mathrm{cond}(AB) \le \mathrm{cond}(A)\,\mathrm{cond}(B)$ and find an example with strict inequality.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Submultiplicativity applied to $AB$ and $(AB)^{-1} = B^{-1}A^{-1}$.

Step 2: Proof
$\mathrm{cond}(AB) = \|AB\|\|B^{-1}A^{-1}\| \le \|A\|\|B\|\|B^{-1}\|\|A^{-1}\| = \mathrm{cond}(A)\mathrm{cond}(B)$.

Step 3: Equality
$A = \mathrm{diag}(1, 2)$, $B = \mathrm{diag}(1, 3)$: $AB = \mathrm{diag}(1, 6)$, $\mathrm{cond} = 6 = 2\cdot 3$.

Step 4: Strict
$A = \begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$, $B = A^{-1} = \begin{pmatrix}1&-1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$: $AB = I$, $\mathrm{cond}(AB) = 1$, but $\mathrm{cond}_\infty(A) = 2\cdot 2 = 4$, $\mathrm{cond}(B) = 4$: $1 < 16$.

Step 5: Takeaway: What matters
Factors can “heal” each other – the inequality is only an upper bound. Important for decompositions $A = LU$.

exercises.title: Perturbed matrix
exercises.description: For $A = \begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1.0001\end{pmatrix}$ the entry $a_{22}$ is perturbed by $10^{-4}$ to $1.0002$; $b = (2, 2.0001)^T$. Compute the perturbed solution and check $\frac{\|\Delta x\|}{\|x\|} \le \mathrm{cond}(A)\frac{\|\Delta A\|}{\|A\|}$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Solve the new system with $\tilde A = \begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1.0002\end{pmatrix}$.

Step 3: Changes
$\Delta x = \tilde x - x = (0.5, -0.5)^T$, $\frac{\|\Delta x\|_\infty}{\|x\|_\infty} = 0.5$. $\frac{\|\Delta A\|_\infty}{\|A\|_\infty} = \frac{10^{-4}}{2.0001} = 5\cdot10^{-5}$.

Step 4: Check
Right-hand side: $40004\cdot 5\cdot10^{-5} = 2.0$. (Strictly speaking $\|x + \Delta x\|$ is in the denominator: $\frac{0.5}{1.5} = 0.33 \le 2$ ✓.)

Step 5: Takeaway: What matters
A perturbation of $0.005\%$ in one matrix entry changes the solution by $50\%$ – again the effect of the condition.

exercises.title: Proving the row-sum norm
exercises.description: Prove that the matrix norm induced by $\|\cdot\|_\infty$ is $\|A\|_\infty = \max_i\sum_j|a_{ij}|$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Two directions: an upper bound for all $x$, then a vector that attains it.

Step 2: Upper bound
For $\|x\|_\infty = 1$: $|(Ax)_i| = |\sum_ja_{ij}x_j| \le \sum_j|a_{ij}||x_j| \le \sum_j|a_{ij}|$. So $\|Ax\|_\infty \le \max_i\sum_j|a_{ij}|$.

Step 3: Choosing the vector
Let $k$ be the row with maximal magnitude sum. Choose $x_j = \mathrm{sign}(a_{kj})$ (or $1$ if $a_{kj} = 0$). Then $\|x\|_\infty = 1$.

Step 4: Attained
$(Ax)_k = \sum_ja_{kj}\,\mathrm{sign}(a_{kj}) = \sum_j|a_{kj}|$. So $\|Ax\|_\infty \ge \sum_j|a_{kj}| = \max_i\sum_j|a_{ij}|$.

Step 5: Conclusion
Both directions together: $\|A\|_\infty = \max_{\|x\|_\infty = 1}\|Ax\|_\infty = \max_i\sum_j|a_{ij}|$. Example $A = \begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{pmatrix}$: row 2, $x = (1,1)^T$, $Ax = (3, 7)^T$, $\|Ax\|_\infty = 7$ ✓.

Step 6: Takeaway: What matters
Pattern: upper bound + example vector attaining it. The maximising vector consists of the signs of the critical row.

exercises.title: cond₂ = σ_max/σ_min
exercises.description: Show that $\mathrm{cond}_2(A) = \sigma_{\max}/\sigma_{\min}$ with singular values $\sigma_i = \sqrt{\lambda_i(A^TA)}$ and compute $\mathrm{cond}_2$ for $A = \begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{pmatrix}$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
$\|A\|_2 = \sigma_{\max}$; for $A^{-1}$ we have $(A^{-1})^TA^{-1} = (AA^T)^{-1}$.

Step 2: Norm of A⁻¹
$AA^T$ and $A^TA$ have the same eigenvalues. The eigenvalues of $(AA^T)^{-1}$ are $1/\sigma_i^2$, the largest is $1/\sigma_{\min}^2$. So $\|A^{-1}\|_2 = 1/\sigma_{\min}$.

Step 3: Product
$\mathrm{cond}_2(A) = \|A\|_2\|A^{-1}\|_2 = \sigma_{\max}/\sigma_{\min}$.

Step 4: Numbers
$A^TA = \begin{pmatrix}10&14\\14&20\end{pmatrix}$, $\lambda = 15 \pm\sqrt{221} = 29.866,\ 0.1339$. $\sigma = 5.465,\ 0.3660$. $\mathrm{cond}_2 = 14.93$.

Step 5: Takeaway: What matters
The 2-norm condition is the ratio of the largest to the smallest distortion of the unit ball – geometrically intuitive.

exercises.title: Deriving the perturbation theorem
exercises.description: Derive $\frac{\|\Delta x\|}{\|x\|} \le \mathrm{cond}(A)\frac{\|\Delta b\|}{\|b\|}$ for $A(x + \Delta x) = b + \Delta b$ and show that the bound can be sharp.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Subtract $Ax = b$ and use compatibility of the norms.

Step 2: Difference equation
$A\Delta x = \Delta b \Rightarrow \Delta x = A^{-1}\Delta b \Rightarrow \|\Delta x\| \le \|A^{-1}\|\|\Delta b\|$.

Step 3: Denominator
$b = Ax \Rightarrow \|b\| \le \|A\|\|x\| \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{\|x\|} \le \dfrac{\|A\|}{\|b\|}$.

Step 4: Combining
$\dfrac{\|\Delta x\|}{\|x\|} \le \|A^{-1}\|\|\Delta b\|\cdot\dfrac{\|A\|}{\|b\|} = \mathrm{cond}(A)\dfrac{\|\Delta b\|}{\|b\|}$.

Step 5: Sharpness
Equality holds when $x$ is chosen with $\|b\| = \|A\|\|x\|$ ($x$ “maximally stretched”) and $\Delta b$ such that $\|A^{-1}\Delta b\| = \|A^{-1}\|\|\Delta b\|$ ($\Delta b$ “maximally stretched by $A^{-1}$”). For $A = \mathrm{diag}(1, 10^{-4})$, $b = (1, 0)$, $\Delta b = (0, \varepsilon)$ the bound is attained exactly.

Step 6: Takeaway: What matters
So the condition number is the smallest constant valid for all $b, \Delta b$ – it is not just a bound but the “worst-case ratio”.

exercises.title: cond₂(AᵀA) = cond₂(A)²
exercises.description: Show $\mathrm{cond}_2(A^TA) = \mathrm{cond}_2(A)^2$ and check it for $A = \begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&0.1\end{pmatrix}$ ($\mathrm{cond}_2(A) \approx 20.05$).
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
$A^TA$ is symmetric positive definite with eigenvalues $\sigma_i^2$.

Step 2: Proof
For spd matrices $\mathrm{cond}_2 = \lambda_{\max}/\lambda_{\min}$. So $\mathrm{cond}_2(A^TA) = \sigma_{\max}^2/\sigma_{\min}^2 = \bigl(\sigma_{\max}/\sigma_{\min}\bigr)^2 = \mathrm{cond}_2(A)^2$.

Step 3: Numerical example
$A^TA = \begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1.01\end{pmatrix}$, $\lambda = 2.00501,\ 0.00499$. $\mathrm{cond}_2(A^TA) = 402.0$.

Step 4: Comparison
$\mathrm{cond}_2(A)^2 = 20.05^2 = 402.0$ ✓.

Step 5: Consequence
Normal equations $A^TAx = A^Tb$ (4.5) square the condition: for $\mathrm{cond}(A) = 10^8$ this becomes $10^{16}$ – unsolvable in double precision. That is why QR is preferred.

Step 6: Takeaway: What matters
Be careful when forming $A^TA$: the condition is squared, information is lost.

exercises.title: Deriving norm-equivalence constants
exercises.description: Prove $\|x\|_\infty \le \|x\|_2 \le \sqrt n\|x\|_\infty$ and $\|x\|_2 \le \|x\|_1 \le \sqrt n\|x\|_2$ and give vectors for which equality holds.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
First chain: sum of squares against the largest entry. Second chain: Cauchy–Schwarz.

Step 2: ∞ ≤ 2 ≤ √n·∞
$\|x\|_\infty^2 = \max x_i^2 \le \sum x_i^2 = \|x\|_2^2 \le n\max x_i^2 = n\|x\|_\infty^2$. Take roots.

Step 3: 2 ≤ 1
$\|x\|_1^2 = \bigl(\sum|x_i|\bigr)^2 = \sum x_i^2 + \sum_{i\ne j}|x_i||x_j| \ge \sum x_i^2 = \|x\|_2^2$.

Step 4: 1 ≤ √n·2
Cauchy–Schwarz: $\|x\|_1 = \sum 1\cdot|x_i| \le \sqrt{\sum 1^2}\sqrt{\sum x_i^2} = \sqrt n\|x\|_2$.

Step 6: Takeaway: What matters
The constants are optimal. They grow with $\sqrt n$ – in high dimensions norms are “far apart”.

exercises.title: The Frobenius norm is not induced
exercises.description: Show that $\|A\|_F = \sqrt{\sum a_{ij}^2}$ is not an induced norm but is compatible with $\|\cdot\|_2$: $\|Ax\|_2 \le \|A\|_F\|x\|_2$. Compare $\|A\|_F$ and $\|A\|_2$ for $A = \begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{pmatrix}$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Every induced norm satisfies $\|I\| = 1$. Check that for $\|\cdot\|_F$.

Step 2: Not induced
$\|I_n\|_F = \sqrt{n} \ne 1$ for $n \ge 2$. So not an induced norm.

Step 3: Compatibility
Cauchy–Schwarz in each row: $|(Ax)_i| \le \|a_i\|_2\|x\|_2$. Squaring and summing: $\|Ax\|_2^2 \le \sum_i\|a_i\|_2^2\|x\|_2^2 = \|A\|_F^2\|x\|_2^2$.

Step 4: Numbers
$\|A\|_F = \sqrt{1 + 4 + 9 + 16} = \sqrt{30} = 5.477$, $\|A\|_2 = 5.465$. In general $\|A\|_2 \le \|A\|_F \le \sqrt{\mathrm{rank}}\,\|A\|_2$.

Step 5: Takeaway: What matters
$\|A\|_F^2 = \sum\sigma_i^2$ (sum of squared singular values) – easy to compute, hence often used as a substitute for $\|A\|_2$.

exercises.title: Analysing iterative refinement
exercises.description: Let $\tilde x = (2, 0)^T$ be an inaccurate solution of $Ax = b$ with $A = \begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1.0001\end{pmatrix}$, $b = (2, 2.0001)^T$. Perform one refinement step and explain when it helps.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Idea: $x = \tilde x + d$ with $Ad = b - A\tilde x = r$.

Step 4: New solution
$\hat x = \tilde x + d = (1, 1)^T$ – exact.

Step 5: When does it help?
Crucial: $r$ must be computed accurately (higher precision), otherwise it is itself cancellation ($b$ and $A\tilde x$ almost equal). Convergence per step by a factor of about $\mathrm{cond}(A)\cdot u$: only for $\mathrm{cond}(A)\,u < 1$.

Step 6: Takeaway: What matters
Iterative refinement repairs rounding errors of the method, not a singular matrix.

exercises.title: Scaling / equilibration
exercises.description: Compute $\mathrm{cond}_\infty$ for $A = \begin{pmatrix}1&10^4\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$ and for the row-scaled matrix $\hat A = \begin{pmatrix}10^{-4}&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$ (row 1 multiplied by $10^{-4}$).
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Overview: What is asked?
Determine both inverses explicitly (2×2).

Step 4: Consequence
The condition drops from $10^4$ to $4$ – merely by multiplying one equation by a factor (an equivalent system; the right-hand side is scaled too). The solution stays the same.

Step 5: Limit
Scaling helps only if the bad state is caused by scales (“apparently ill-conditioned”). The matrix $\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1.0001\end{pmatrix}$ cannot be saved this way.

Step 6: Takeaway: What matters
Before solving bring rows/columns to similar magnitudes (equilibration) – especially for data with different units.
